novelty_audits.summary: Result (general-k e_k*e_r, k-fold coset-sum / Jing identification, two-column GF) is NEW. k=1 plethystic-Y_1 precedent: OBW24 (2410.13642) Prop 5.4 and Ion-Wu 2011.12189 Prop 6.32 (+ Thm 7.13), stable limit, single Y_1 only. The kernel (K_k) alone is classical: Macdonald SF&HP III (2.2) (HL P_lambda at lambda=(1^k)). Also checked: SZ00, Bhattacharya, Venkateswaran - clear.

tree.approach: Run the Day 207b outer-peel induction on the two-variable GF Gamma_0 = E(z)E(w); fit and prove a closed two-column rule (TC).

children.approach: (TC) sum_{a,b} z^a w^b t^{-C(k,2)} e_k(Y).(e_a e_b) = sum_{b0+n1+n2=k} sum_{i<=n1,j<=n2} s^{2b0+(n1-i)+(n2-j)} t^{-b0(i+j)-(n1-i)j-(n2-j)i} K_ij(z,w) N^(n1)_i N^(n2)_j z^{-n1} w^{-n2} e_{b0} E(t^i z)E(t^j w), K_ij = prod_{p<i}(t^p z - s w)/(t^p z - t^j w) prod_{r<j}(s z - t^r w)/(t^i z - t^r w), N^(n)_j = t^{-nj}c(n,j). Fitted on symbolic Gamma_1..Gamma_3 (fit_structure.py); checked vs direct AHA exactly at 3 random rational points for all m<=6, k<=4, and at (m,k)=(6,5),(7,4),(7,5) (check_conj.py; k=4,5 out of sample).
Stub: one-column e_k*e_r Pieri theorem (A_k kernel, K_k chain, E_k outer-peel + (*)), Day 207b; canonical node carries the proof.

BLOCKING sub-claim: closing identity for the two-variable outer-peel step (analogue of Day 207b (*)); every other step of gf_recursion.py is a proved Day 207b lemma. Proving it promotes (TC) to proved by outer-peel induction.

Kill test: outer-peel on E(z)E(w) yields only chain shifts e_{b0} E(t^i z)E(t^j w), b0+i+j<=k (C(k+3,3) terms), support l(lambda)<=3; no non-chain Q-product appears, so the kill criterion did NOT fire. Symbolic for k<=3 (gf_recursion.py), k=4,5 via (TC); checked vs direct AHA m<=4, k<=3.
children.caveat: Coefficients carry cross poles at z = t^c w (from partial-fractioning in Lemma 2) that cancel only in the total and cannot be absorbed into the shifts; the e-expansion has an unbounded tail sum_q T_lambda(t^q) e_lambda e_q e_{N-q} of length ~min(a,b), T(q)+T(N-q)=0 (tails.py, folded.py; verified vs AHA a,b<=4). No bounded-length e-expansion; GF rule is closed.
